title: Adaptive evolution of polyploid crops.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: Europe PMC flags show no open access, no PMCID, no supplement, no data or database cross-references, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI links (GEO/SRA/BioProject), and no Zenodo/Dryad hits on the DOI.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Abstract only: the paper says itself that it is a Review that synthesizes how polyploidy (having more than two sets of chromosomes) shapes crop evolution. It reports no new measurements.

a1_downloadable.note: No dataset exists. This is a narrative Review with no accessions, supplement or repository deposit (checked through Europe PMC, NCBI links and a DOI search on Zenodo/Dryad).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no table, so there is no label column. Any label would have to be pulled together from the primary studies the Review cites.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable, because there is no data.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: There are no counts to compare.

honest_claim_h3: None possible: the paper contributes no data to model.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use duplicated-gene features in polyploid crop genomes to predict which gene copies diverge in function; considered and dropped.
plain_idea.train_on: Nothing from this paper. A Review has no examples; it would mean collecting gene-copy data from the cited primary studies (count unknown).
plain_idea.predict: Whether a duplicated gene copy keeps, splits or loses its function. No measured labels come with this paper.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Crop breeders working with wheat, cotton or potato could rank gene copies to target, but primary datasets would be needed, not this Review.

ml_idea: None from this paper. Any polyploid-crop ML project should start from a primary dataset, such as a homoeolog (matching gene copies from different ancestral genomes) expression atlas.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because there is no data.
